summary: Two range lights marked Mabou Harbour from 1884; wooden towers built in 1908 replaced the mast lights. The 1908 tower is a federal heritage building (2004).

structures.role: rear range tower (the tower standing today)

structures.status: removed from pier 1892; carried away by gale 1904

access.note: LighthouseFriends lists the grounds and tower as open. No source says the tower may be climbed.

facts.agency: Canadian Coast Guard (LighthouseFriends); the Coast Guard List of Lights calls the light a private aid, seasonal

events.note: Two range lights put in operation on 15 July 1884 (front fixed white, rear fixed red)
Front light taken off the south pier at the close of navigation because the pier was in poor repair; replaced the next spring
Gale on the night of 14 November 1904 carried away the mast and shed of the front light; a temporary pole light was used

Enclosed square wooden towers replaced the mast lights, built under contract by E. C. Embree of Port Hawkesbury for $2,450 (LighthouseFriends gives 1908; the 1909 report describes the finished towers)
A December storm tore most of one wall off the front range tower
Red steel skeletal tower put up to show the front light; the wooden front tower was demolished
Rear light electrified in August 1966 and made unwatched
Front light discontinued on 9 November 1987; the 1908 rear tower became the only light, guiding boats toward the wharf

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's 1908 (Wikidata) and 1884 (Rowlett) are both supported for different structures. Two range lights were first lit in 1884 on masts; the wooden towers standing now were built in 1908.

The record's point (46.0859 N, 61.4653 W) agrees with the Coast Guard list position for H1216.1 (46 05 09.2 N, 061 27 55.2 W). The register's rounded point (46.087 N, 61.472 W) lies about half a kilometre to the west. The record's point is kept.
The Coast Guard list calls the light a private aid and seasonal; LighthouseFriends says the Coast Guard owns it. The story states both and leaves the question open.
The register gives 18 March 2004; LighthouseFriends gives 2006. The story gives the register date and notes LighthouseFriends' 2006. Not resolved.

notes_for_editor: (1) Keepers: the roster is LighthouseFriends' list, the only complete list found; Canada has no USLHS roster. Doyle is matched to the front light by position in the 1906 OCR keeper table (scan p.181, printed p.172): the OCR row reads 'Doyle, Edward / Mabou Front Range Light / June'. The 1906 page image (read at reduced scale) is a clean table with station and name in aligned rows, but I could not isolate Doyle's own row on it. The same row is legible on the 1905 report's keeper list (scan p.343, printed p.262) as 'Doyle, Edward / Mabou Front Range Light / June 14, 1897'. The 1909 keeper table lists 'Mabou Outer' and 'M Inner' with E. Doyle and Roderick McLean in matching positions, which fits the front and rear assignment (position match only, not cited). (2) The 1909 report's heading at the Mabou entry is OCR'd as 'Mahon.'. The page image (scan p.63, printed p.56) reads 'Mabou.'. The contractor, price, tower heights and the range-mast wording agree with LighthouseFriends' account of the same towers. (3) Recognition date: the register gives 18 March 2004; LighthouseFriends gives 2006. The story states both. (4) LighthouseFriends dates the Embree contract to 1908; the 1909 report describes the finished towers. The story says both. (5) Ownership: the Coast Guard's list says 'Private aid' and 'Seasonal'; LighthouseFriends says the Coast Guard owns it. Not resolved. (6) The 1884 figures come from LighthouseFriends quoting the Department's announcement; the 1884 report is not in the local corpus. (7) The 1964 storm and the 1965 steel tower are LighthouseFriends only. (8) A Chronicling America search for 'Mabou' with 'lighthouse' returned nothing relevant. (9) The record's 'tower open' note from the Lighthouse Directory was not checked; the story uses LighthouseFriends' 'grounds/tower open' with a note that no source says the tower may be climbed.
